guard: both OpenCode plugins hand a once task over at most once: the drive claims it right before the submission and releases it when the submission fails, and the 1.x plugin's teardown is the exit a once seat takes on its own
why: M1 and M3 drop the release from a failed submission. The task stays claimed, so it is neither
sealed nor reported, and the manager learns nothing until the handoff timer fires.
M2 drops the 1.x claim. The release then seals nothing, the task stays offerable, and the error
retry sends it a second time: the duplicate run this feature exists to prevent.
M4 drops the 2.x claim. A native prompt typed while the submission is in flight peeks the task as
still pending and carries it too.
M5 drops the 1.x exit registration, so a once seat whose report cannot land has no teardown to run.

mutations.name: M1 a failed 1.x submission no longer releases the task it carried
mutations.expectRed: 1.x: a failed submission seals the task it carried

mutations.name: M2 the 1.x drive sends the task without claiming it
mutations.expectRed: 1.x: the retry after the failure does not submit the sealed task again

mutations.name: M3 a failed 2.x submission no longer releases the task it carried
mutations.expectRed: 2.x: a failed submission seals the task it carried

mutations.name: M4 the 2.x drive sends the task without claiming it
mutations.expectRed: 2.x: a native prompt meanwhile does not carry the claimed task

mutations.name: M5 the 1.x plugin registers no once exit
mutations.expectRed: 1.x: the registered once exit runs the plugin's teardown and exits 1
